# p0_looker_ai (Resource)

A Looker installation for agentic access.

Installing it allows P0 to grant agents just-in-time access to the LookML models of a Looker (Google Cloud core) instance. Each grant gets a Looker service account of its own, which P0 deletes when the grant ends.

**Important:** Before creating this resource you must stage the installation with `p0_looker_ai_staged`, deploy the connector's Cloud Run service, and add the Looker Admin key as a version of the Admin key's secret. Creating this resource runs P0's install check, which signs in to the instance with that key through the connector, so the check fails until the version exists.

**Note:** This integration is currently in preview.

For the full install steps, see [Looker](https://docs.p0.dev/integrations/resource-integrations/agentic-gateway/mcp-server/looker).

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Installs Looker for agentic access, with P0's Looker connector on Cloud Run
# and the instance's Admin key in Google Secret Manager.
# Full chain: p0_gcp -> p0_looker_ai_staged -> Admin key secret -> Admin key
# version (added outside Terraform) -> Cloud Run connector -> p0_looker_ai.
#
# Order matters. Creating p0_looker_ai runs P0's install check, which signs in
# to Looker with the Admin key through the connector. So the key must be in its
# secret before p0_looker_ai is created. Apply in three steps:
#
#   1. Create the Admin key's secret:
#        terraform apply -target=google_secret_manager_secret.admin_key
#   2. Add the Admin key as a version of that secret, with the gcloud command
#      shown above the secret below.
#   3. Create everything else:
#        terraform apply

resource "p0_gcp" "example" {
  organization_id = "123456789012"
}

locals {
  project  = "my-project-id"
  instance = "acme"
}

resource "google_project_service" "enable_services" {
  for_each = toset([
    "cloudresourcemanager.googleapis.com",
    "iam.googleapis.com",
    "run.googleapis.com",
    "secretmanager.googleapis.com",
  ])
  project            = local.project
  service            = each.key
  disable_on_destroy = false
}

# Holds the Looker API key of a Looker service account with the Admin role.
# Only a Looker admin can create that account and its key. The key never goes
# through Terraform, so it never lands in the Terraform state. Add it as a
# version of this secret after step 1 above, as JSON:
#
#   printf '{"client_id":"%s","client_secret":"%s"}' "$LOOKER_CLIENT_ID" "$LOOKER_CLIENT_SECRET" \
#     | gcloud secrets versions add p0_install_looker_acme_admin-key \
#       --project=my-project-id --data-file=-
resource "google_secret_manager_secret" "admin_key" {
  project   = local.project
  secret_id = "p0_install_looker_${local.instance}_admin-key"

  replication {
    auto {}
  }

  depends_on = [google_project_service.enable_services]
}

resource "p0_looker_ai_staged" "example" {
  id               = local.instance
  instance_url     = "https://acme.looker.app"
  admin_key_secret = google_secret_manager_secret.admin_key.secret_id

  secret_manager = {
    type       = "gcp-sm"
    project_id = local.project
  }

  depends_on = [p0_gcp.example]
}

resource "google_service_account" "connector" {
  project      = local.project
  account_id   = split("@", p0_looker_ai_staged.example.secret_manager.connector_service_account)[0]
  display_name = "P0 Cloud Run Looker connector"

  depends_on = [google_project_service.enable_services]
}

resource "google_cloud_run_v2_service" "connector" {
  project             = local.project
  name                = p0_looker_ai_staged.example.secret_manager.connector_service_name
  location            = p0_looker_ai_staged.example.secret_manager.connector_region
  deletion_protection = false
  # P0 calls the connector from outside GCP, so IAM, not origin, gates access.
  ingress = "INGRESS_TRAFFIC_ALL"

  template {
    service_account = google_service_account.connector.email

    containers {
      # PLACEHOLDER: the Looker connector image isn't published yet. Pin it by
      # tag and digest (<tag>@sha256:<digest>) once it is.
      image = "docker.io/p0security/p0-connector-looker-ai-gcloud:unpublished"

      # The connector also checks this against the caller's OIDC token.
      env {
        name  = "INVOKER_SA_EMAIL"
        value = p0_gcp.example.service_account_email
      }
    }
  }

  depends_on = [google_project_service.enable_services]
}

resource "google_cloud_run_v2_service_iam_member" "invoke_connector" {
  project  = local.project
  location = google_cloud_run_v2_service.connector.location
  name     = google_cloud_run_v2_service.connector.name
  role     = "roles/run.invoker"
  member   = "serviceAccount:${p0_gcp.example.service_account_email}"
}

# P0 reads the service to get its invocation URL while it installs. The invoker
# role gives run.routes.invoke only, so it cannot do this read.
resource "google_cloud_run_v2_service_iam_member" "read_connector" {
  project  = local.project
  location = google_cloud_run_v2_service.connector.location
  name     = google_cloud_run_v2_service.connector.name
  role     = "roles/run.viewer"
  member   = "serviceAccount:${p0_gcp.example.service_account_email}"
}

data "google_project" "this" {
  project_id = local.project
}

# The connector keeps each grant's Looker API key in its own secret. GCP checks
# secretmanager.secrets.create on the project, so this binding has no condition.
resource "google_project_iam_custom_role" "connector_secret_create" {
  project     = local.project
  role_id     = "p0LookerConnectorSecretCreate"
  title       = "P0 Looker connector secret creation"
  permissions = ["secretmanager.secrets.create"]

  depends_on = [google_project_service.enable_services]
}

resource "google_project_iam_member" "connector_secret_create" {
  project = local.project
  role    = google_project_iam_custom_role.connector_secret_create.name
  member  = "serviceAccount:${google_service_account.connector.email}"
}

# The connector writes each grant's key and deletes the secret when the grant
# ends. It never reads a grant secret back.
resource "google_project_iam_custom_role" "connector_secret_manage" {
  project = local.project
  role_id = "p0LookerConnectorSecretManage"
  title   = "P0 Looker connector grant secret management"
  permissions = [
    "secretmanager.secrets.delete",
    "secretmanager.versions.add",
  ]

  depends_on = [google_project_service.enable_services]
}

resource "google_project_iam_member" "connector_secret_manage" {
  project = local.project
  role    = google_project_iam_custom_role.connector_secret_manage.name
  member  = "serviceAccount:${google_service_account.connector.email}"

  # P0 names the grant secrets with this prefix. IAM conditions use the project
  # number, not the project ID.
  condition {
    title      = "P0 Looker grant secrets"
    expression = "resource.name.startsWith('projects/${data.google_project.this.number}/secrets/p0_access-token_looker_${local.instance}_')"
  }
}

# The connector reads the Admin key on every call. Grant it on this secret
# alone: P0 names the secret in each call, so any other secret the connector
# can read is one a call could point it at.
resource "google_secret_manager_secret_iam_member" "admin_key" {
  project   = local.project
  secret_id = google_secret_manager_secret.admin_key.secret_id
  role      = "roles/secretmanager.secretAccessor"
  member    = "serviceAccount:${google_service_account.connector.email}"
}

# The accessor role gives secretmanager.versions.access only. The connector also
# reads the version's metadata, so the Admin key needs this grant as well.
resource "google_secret_manager_secret_iam_member" "admin_key_read" {
  project   = local.project
  secret_id = google_secret_manager_secret.admin_key.secret_id
  role      = "roles/secretmanager.viewer"
  member    = "serviceAccount:${google_service_account.connector.email}"
}

# Completes the install. Create it only once the Admin key is in its secret
# (step 2 above): P0's install check signs in to Looker with that key.
resource "p0_looker_ai" "example" {
  id               = p0_looker_ai_staged.example.id
  instance_url     = p0_looker_ai_staged.example.instance_url
  admin_key_secret = p0_looker_ai_staged.example.admin_key_secret
  # Optional. The Looker folder that agents save content to, from its URL
  # (/folders/<ID>). Without it, content that an agent saves goes to Trash when
  # its grant ends.
  content_folder_id = "42"

  secret_manager = {
    type       = p0_looker_ai_staged.example.secret_manager.type
    project_id = p0_looker_ai_staged.example.secret_manager.project_id
  }

  depends_on = [
    google_cloud_run_v2_service_iam_member.invoke_connector,
    google_cloud_run_v2_service_iam_member.read_connector,
    google_project_iam_member.connector_secret_create,
    google_project_iam_member.connector_secret_manage,
    google_secret_manager_secret_iam_member.admin_key,
    google_secret_manager_secret_iam_member.admin_key_read,
  ]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `admin_key_secret` (String) The ID of the Google Secret Manager secret, in `secret_manager.project_id`, that holds the Looker API key of a Looker service account with the Admin role. Only the connector reads it, never P0. Must match the `p0_looker_ai_staged` resource.
- `id` (String) The `id` of the `p0_looker_ai_staged` resource being finalized
- `instance_url` (String) The base URL of the Looker (Google Cloud core) instance, `https://<name>.looker.app`, in lowercase with no path or trailing slash. P0 reaches the instance over the internet, so it needs a public endpoint. Custom domains and ports aren't supported. Must match the `p0_looker_ai_staged` resource.
- `secret_manager` (Attributes) Where P0's Looker connector runs and where the Looker instance's Admin key is stored (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--secret_manager))

### Optional

- `content_folder_id` (String) The ID of the Looker folder that agents save content to, the last part of its URL (`/folders/<ID>`). An edit grant gets edit access to it, and content saved there outlives the grant. Without a folder, content that an agent saves goes to Trash when its grant ends. Once set, it can be changed to another folder but not removed.

### Read-Only

- `state` (String) This item's install progress in the P0 application:
	- 'stage': The item has been staged for installation
	- 'configure': The item is available to be added to P0, and may be configured
	- 'installed': The item is fully installed

<a id="nestedatt--secret_manager"></a>
### Nested Schema for `secret_manager`

Required:

- `project_id` (String) The GCP project that hosts the connector's Cloud Run service and the secret that holds the Looker instance's Admin key. Must match the `p0_looker_ai_staged` resource.
- `type` (String) The secret manager that stores the Looker instance's Admin key. Only `gcp-sm` (Google Secret Manager) is supported. Must match the `p0_looker_ai_staged` resource.

Read-Only:

- `connector_region` (String) The GCP region in which to deploy the connector's Cloud Run service
- `connector_service_account` (String) The email of the GCP service account that the connector must run as
- `connector_service_name` (String) The name to give the connector's Cloud Run service
- `connector_service_uri` (String) The invocation URL of the connector's Cloud Run service, resolved by P0 during install
